ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RELEASE POLICIES

The MPLX Terminals, LLC- Louisville Kramers Lane LP Terminal is an on-shore, bulk petroleum terminal used in the storage and distribution of refined petroleum products to retail and commercial end-users in the vicinity of Louisville, KY. The Terminal handles and stores various grades of unleaded gasoline, low sulfur diesel/#2 fuel oil, butane, ethanol, and various other petroleum-based additives.

The Louisville- Kramers Lane LP Terminal is committed to operating and maintaining processes in a safe, reliable and environmentally sound manner. MPLX believes that excellent performance in health, safety, and the environment (HES) goes hand-in-hand with operating reliably, and that outstanding HES performance is of paramount importance.

The Terminal is designed, operated and maintained in a manner that protects the environment, as well as the health and safety of its employees, contractors and the community. MPLX promotes health, safety, and the environment through programs of awareness, compliance, prevention and protection. These programs include a combination of accidental release prevention/mitigation and emergency response planning. This document provides a brief overview of the comprehensive risk management activities that MPLX has designed and implemented, including:

A. A description of the facility and the use of regulated substances.
B. An overview of the accidental release prevention programs.
C. A five-year accident history for accidental releases of regulated substances.
D. An overview of the emergency response program.
E. An overview of planned changes to improve safety.

A. STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES

The Butane Blending Process has been classified as Program Level 3. No Program Level 1 or 2 processes containing regulated substances are identified. By virtue of its flammable hazards , it's necessary to observe certain safety precautions in handling butane to prevent unnecessary

human exposure, reduce the threat to employee health, and minimize the threat and impact to nearby members of the community.  Safety at the Facility depends upon the manner in which butane is handled as well as the various safety devices incorporated into the design of the process. Furthermore, comprehensive training is provided to employees, which reinforces the safety policies and procedures while operating the Butane Blending Process.

The Butane Blending Process is both a continuous fuel (gasoline) blending process feeding the refined products load rack and a batch-type process (tank blending) based on seasonal regulatory Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP)/distillation property adjustments. Butane is received by truck (transports), stored on-site in a single pressure vessel, and piped to a metered injection skid and subsequent injection points feeding the refined product load rack (primary blend method) and  an on-site gasoline storage tank. Process safety controls include "Smart-Hoses", low emission couplers, emergency shutoff/fire valves (ESVs) throughout (manual, automated and thermally actuated), vessel PRVs, excess flow valves, hydrostatic pressure relief, and process area hydrocarbon detectors along with on-site fixed fire water monitors. Access to the Louisville-Kramers Lane LP Terminal and butane offload/storage area is restricted to authorized employees, management personnel and authorized contractors/visitors/haulers.

B. GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL-SPECIFIC PREVENTION MEASURES

The Louisville- Kramers Lane LP Terminal accidental release prevention programs and emergency planning/response programs help effectively manage the hazards posed by butane to the Terminal employees, surrounding public, and environment. The covered process is regulated by the EPA RMP regulation 40 CFR Part 68, as well as the OSHA Process Safety Management standard 29 CFR 1910.119. The following accident prevention program elements are in place at the Louis

ocarbon Detectors with automatic process shutdown functions; 
-Strategically located valves to isolate leaks; and
-"Smart-Hoses" with design break-away and self-closing valves on each end.

General Emergency Response

-Emergency alert system;
-Periodic emergency training for employees;
-Communication systems with local emergency responders and regulatory agencies; and
-Emergency drills/exercises with Terminal personnel, regulatory agencies, and community emergency responders to enhance response skills and coordination among agencies.

Further, the Louisville-Kramers Lane LP Terminal complies with the National Fire Protection Association's (NFPA's) Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) Code (NFPA-58) requirements for LP Gas Systems. In addition to the presence of appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of butane, a Facility Response Plan (SMARTPLAN) is in place for the location with response activities being coordinated with the Pleasure Ridge Park (PRP) Fire District and Louisville Metro Emergency Management.

C. FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

The Louisville- Kramers Lane LP Terminal has an excellent record of accident prevention. The Terminal maintains records for all incidental (including near misses) and significant chemical releases inclusive of any root cause analyses and associated, follow-up actions.  As this is a new process, there have been no reportable (as defined in the EPA RMP regulations) accidents within the past five (5) years.

D. EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

The Facility's emergency response plans are coordinated with the PRP Fire District and Louisville Metro Emergency Management (Jefferson County LEPC.)  The SMARTPLAN instructs employees what to do in case of a release, fire, and to notify emergency responders when there is a need for a response.

The Facility (Non-Responding Stationary Source) maintains (annual training) incipient fire and HAZWOPER 1st Responder Operations capabilities.

The PRP Fire District and Louisville Metro Emergency Managem

ent participate in annual butane coordination/training and notification sessions for this process.

Addition exercises including Tabletop and/or Full-Scale are performed as agreed upon between responding agencies and the Facility.

E. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY

MPLX is continually striving to make the Louisville- Kramers Lane LP Terminal the safest and most reliable workplace possible for its employees, neighbors and the community.

In an effort to improve and promote system safety, MPLX actively seeks employee input on process safety improvements. All Process Safety Events (as identified in API 754) are electronically recorded, reviewed, and/or investigated via a root cause analysis (TapRooT) per Marathon policy.
